title: Lesson 20: General Systems Architecture: Environments and CI/CD in ML and AI Pipelines
description: The same environment-and-release discipline from Lesson 19, applied to machine learning and AI systems. Why the ML artifact is more than code (code, data, and model all change), the continuous X's (CI, CD, CT, CM), the MLOps maturity levels, how a model promotes from a development environment to production, and what changes when the artifact is a nondeterministic agent that needs eval gates instead of unit tests.

questions.question: Why is a machine learning release harder to manage than a plain software release?
options: Code, data, and model all ship together, and any can change
It always needs far more compute than an ordinary software build
Its outputs can never be stored in version control at all
It never needs any validation before it reaches production
questions.explanation: The artifact is a bundle rather than a single deployable, so the pipeline must handle three kinds of change plus silent model degradation on live data.

questions.question: At the most automated maturity level for machine learning operations, what does the pipeline do?
options: It retrains automatically but still deploys the trained model by hand
It builds, tests, and deploys data, model, and pipeline automatically
It deploys models but skips data and pipeline validation entirely
It runs every step of the workflow manually inside shared notebooks
questions.explanation: The fully automated level extends continuous integration and delivery to cover data and pipeline components, not just the model.

questions.question: Why does an agentic AI system call for an evaluation suite rather than exact-match tests?
options: Its outputs never vary, so each response can be checked with an exact match
It cannot be deployed to a staging environment before production
It has no training data available to validate behavior against
Its outputs are nondeterministic, so behavior is scored across many cases
questions.explanation: Because a single run never repeats, behavior is judged by scoring across a versioned set of cases instead of asserting one fixed output.
